name: Revolutionary nationalism
summary: Revolutionary nationalism is a label for nationalist movements that pursue independence or national renewal by overthrowing the existing order, typically through armed struggle against colonial or foreign domination. In its mainstream anti-colonial form it ties political independence to economic transformation, mass participation and a people's right to its own history and culture, usually with a socialist or anti-imperialist orientation.
scope: Revolutionary nationalism as the anti-colonial national-liberation current of the 20th century, centred on Amilcar Cabral, whom the scholarship (s5, reviewing Rabaka) calls a revolutionary nationalist, with Frantz Fanon's work as the context s5 names: nationalism pursued by revolution against colonial or neocolonial rule and joined to a social transformation toward decolonial democratic socialism. Other movements that Wikipedia's overview lists under the label (Irish Fenians, Sandino, the Bolivian MNR, the Indian independence revolutionaries, Eritrea, the French Revolution, Italian Fascism, Third Positionists) are not scoped in because no defining source saved here states their positions; because the label is descriptive rather than one doctrine, the answers follow the left anti-colonial strand and many are low-confidence.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Fanon criticises elites pursuing self-interest, and movements emphasise collective sacrifice (class suicide). (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

self-ownership.rationale: Movements stressed collective duty to the struggle yet also freedom from colonial domination; adherents split.

single-common-good.rationale: Unity of the nation is stressed but Fanon wants popular conflict over class; split. (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

socialized-markets.rationale: Cabral allows a freed nation to adopt the structure that suits it; not specified.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Revolutionary nationalism endorses armed national-liberation war, so refusal to fight is not endorsed (Cabral, Fanon accept armed struggle). (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Fanon criticises leader unaccountability. (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

state-harmful.rationale: These movements aim to seize and build a sovereign national state; Cabral expects a state to inherit power and Fanon wants it democratized, not abolished. (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

surveillance-ok.rationale: Never addressed directly; Fanon criticizes party informant networks but revolutionary movements also rely on security measures. (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

vanguard-party.rationale: Cabral calls for a firmly united vanguard, though his vanguard was a national party rather than a proletarian one.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fanon treats violence as liberating, but Cabral framed war as necessity not virtue; split. (Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.3 'Pitfalls of National Consciousness'.)

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, ch.1 'On Violence': 'Europe is literally the creation of the Third World. The riches which are choking it are those plundered from the underdeveloped peoples'; Cabral, 'The Weapon of Theory' (Unity and Struggle ch.14) defines imperialism as piracy that plunders 'the natural and human resources of our peoples'.

missingStatements.text: The petty bourgeoisie that leads independence must give up its class interests and identify with the working masses.
missingStatements.rationale: Cabral's class suicide thesis is a defining claim about who leads national liberation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Cabral's theory of class suicide; too narrow for other ideologies to take a side on.

missingStatements.text: Political independence from a colonial power should be won by armed struggle rather than negotiation.
missingStatements.rationale: Cabral calls armed struggle the normal way of national liberation imposed by imperialist repression.
